classification.difficultyReason: Explain why a sector perimeter formula does not apply to a composite shape.

content.prompt: Explain why you cannot use the formula $P=l+2r$ for this shape.

spec.description: Rectangle joined to a quadrant on its right. Double ticks match the rectangle's horizontal edges. Single ticks match its left edge and the two quadrant radii. The internal vertical radius is dashed red.
spec.mathematics: The quadrant is centred at the upper junction of the rectangle and quadrant. Its vertical radius is internal; the complete outer boundary includes three rectangle edges, the horizontal radius and the quarter-circle arc. No dimensions are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and equality marks are permanent student-visible givens; no answer is drawn.

answer.short: $l+2r$ is the perimeter of a sector. This is not a sector.
answer.worked: The formula $P=l+2r$ adds an arc and two radii. This shape combines a rectangle and a quadrant, so its perimeter includes additional straight edges. The dashed radius is inside the shape and is not part of the perimeter.
